agency: Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
statute_note: "Every person has a right to inspect a public record in the state"; 2 AAC 96 says agencies may not ask about the requester's intended use.
notes: dec.alaska.gov returned 403 to both curl and WebFetch, so the fields come only from search snippets: the form asks for name, organization, mailing address and email, says using it is optional, and gives a 10-working-day initial response; whether fields are mandatory is unknown. HB 377 (2026; would add audio/video/email to 'records' and allow municipal cost recovery) was heard and held on 2026-04-28. It is not an intake change.

agency: Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM)
platform: email only (also fax/mail; eFile is a document search, not a request form)
statute: Code of Ala. § 36-12-40 (as amended by Act 2024-278) https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/code-of-alabama?section=36-12-40
statute_note: "Every resident has a right to inspect and take a copy of any public record of this state" (Act 2024-278 changed 'citizen' to 'resident' and lets custodians ask for reasonable proof of residency such as an Alabama driver license or voter registration; § 36-12-44(f) lets officers answer nonresidents at their discretion).
notes: ADEM page asks only for a written request by email, fax or mail and has no form, so name/address/ID requirements are not stated. Statute wording comes from the Alabama League of Municipalities' Jan 2026 memo and RCFP, because the legislature's code site is JS-only. 2026 Act SB272 (redacting account/tax ID numbers) does not change how requests are taken.

agency: Arkansas Department of Energy and Environment, Division of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
statute_note: "all public records shall be open to inspection and copying by any citizen of the State of Arkansas" (enforced: a 2022 MuckRock response shows E&E denying a request because the requester did not appear to be an Arkansas citizen).
notes: The DEQ page lists email, fax and mail with no form, so required fields are not stated. Justia (403) and the legislature site were not readable, so the statute quote comes from search snippets of Justia and FindLaw and court opinions. Acts 505/922 of 2025 (meetings and penalties) took effect 2025-08-05. They are not 2026 changes and do not change intake.

agency: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ)
platform: custom web form (Records Request Online Form) plus MegaSearch portal; email/fax/mail per legacy page
email_address: recordscenter@azdeq.gov (seen only in a third-party MuckRock thread)
statute_note: "Any person may request to examine or be furnished copies..."; § 39-121: records "open to inspection by any person". Commercial-purpose requests need a statement under § 39-121.03.
notes: Every azdeq.gov host (azdeq.gov, air., legacy.) returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge (403), so I did not try further. Search snippets say the page links an online request form and MegaSearch, and the legacy page asks for name, phone, mailing address/email and nature of request. Mandatory fields, account and captcha could not be checked. No 2026 Arizona intake change found: HB 4056 (fee waiver for legislators) was vetoed.

agency: California Environmental Protection Agency (CalEPA); boards and departments (CARB, State Water Board, DTSC, CalRecycle, DPR, OEHHA) handle their own requests
platform: email only for CalEPA itself (boards use their own channels; e.g. CalRecycle uses GovQA)
statute_note: "every person has a right to inspect any public record, except as hereafter provided"
change_2026: SB 1159 (Cabaldon), signed 2026-09-30 (Ch. 863, Stats. 2026), effective 2027-01-01: 'person'/'member of the public' under the CPRA no longer includes AI systems, automated agents or robots, and agencies may use a verification tool to judge whether a request was AI-generated (volume consistent with a natural person stays protected). AB 1821 (same date) changes CPRA 10/14-day response clocks to business days and adds extension grounds.
notes: CalEPA's page says to email PRARequests@calepa.ca.gov and names no required fields. 'no' for name/address/ID means CalEPA's own channel asks for nothing beyond an email; board portals were not surveyed. leginfo was 403, so the statute wording comes from california.public.law. I have not opened the chaptered text of SB 1159; its details come from a law-firm alert and trackers. SB 1159 status read from law-firm alerts and LegiScan; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked automated reading.

agency: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE)
statute_note: Public records "shall be open for inspection by any person at reasonable times"
notes: cdphe.colorado.gov returned a CloudFront 403 to curl and WebFetch, so channels come from search snippets of the CDPHE public records page and the HMWMD records-review page. SB26-107 (would have lengthened CORA deadlines and allowed full cost recovery for business requests) was postponed indefinitely on 2026-03-05. Not enacted.

agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)
email_address: deep.foia@ct.gov (status and also on the older form); the FOIA Administrator's email is also listed
statute_note: "every person shall have the right to (1) inspect such records promptly ... (3) receive a copy of such records"
notes: Clicking 'Submit Request' on the GovQA portal goes to RequestLogin.aspx: 'If this is your first online request, please create an account', with email+password login. No guest path was seen, and I did not create an account, so the form's fields are unknown. The portal CSS styles a CAPTCHA ('Enter CAPTCHA code') for the request form, but I couldn't see it behind the login. The page says written correspondence, email or phone to the FOIA Administrator is available for people with limited internet. 2026 bills SB 466 (longer vexatious-requester bans, AI cited) and SB 325 (AI/FOIA task force) were not enacted per available sources.

agency: District of Columbia Department of Energy & Environment (DOEE)
email_address: doee@dc.gov (general agency address; the page says requests may be sent by email)
statute_note: "Any person has a right to inspect, and at his or her discretion, to copy any public record of a public body"
notes: The portal's 'Submit a Records Request' link (RequestOpen.aspx) goes to a GovQA login page that requires creating an account. No guest path was seen. The DOEE FOIA FAQ lists required information as contact name, email, phone and all property addresses, which is why name='yes'; postal address of the requester is not stated. Email/mail/fax are allowed but 'online will be easier to track'. Pending B26-0670 (data privacy, touches FOIA procedures) is not enacted.

agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC)
platform: NextRequest (the statewide Formstack FOIA form at delaware.gov/foia redirects DNREC requesters to it)
statute_note: "Reasonable access to and reasonable facilities for copying of these records shall not be denied to any citizen"; § 10001 frames the Act around 'the citizens of this State'. Ballotpedia counts DE among states that limit requests to residents.
change_2026: Proposed only: SB 355 (Townsend), a FOIA overhaul draft introduced fall 2026 to get comments (codifies an exemption for unreasonably broad or burdensome requests, among other changes). The sponsor said it won't pass in its current form. No enacted 2026 intake change found.
notes: The NextRequest form config (public JSON) has a mandatory dropdown 'Are you a Delaware resident or a business incorporated in Delaware?' (Yes/No) and a mandatory ESA question. Requester name/address/account settings are loaded client-side and I could not see them without a JS browser. The statewide Formstack form (not used for DNREC) requires name, address and email and loads Google reCAPTCHA on the page.

agency: Florida Department of Environmental Protection (DEP)
platform: email only (self-service search via Oculus and the Information Portal)
statute_note: Custodian "shall permit the record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so"
notes: The DEP page only asks you to 'include your preferred contact information, a clear description... and specific date(s)' to speed processing, and nothing is mandatory, hence 'no'. Search snippets also list PublicRecordsRequests_Regulatory@FloridaDEP.gov. 2026 bills HB 437 and SB 770 (faster response times) died. No ID or AI intake change was found.

agency: Georgia Environmental Protection Division (Department of Natural Resources)
statute_note: "All public records shall be open for personal inspection and copying, except those which by order of a court of this state or by law are specifically exempted from disclosure." No residency words. Read via the AG's copy in a search snippet; Justia was behind a Cloudflare challenge.
change_2026: EPD moved to a new Georgia Open Records Act request system on March 30, 2026. Requests now go through the JustFOIA Open Records Request Portal, and EPD says it no longer accepts requests sent to the old email addresses. No statewide 2026 statute on requester ID, residency or AI was found (SB 482, which would have required in-person notarized requests for bodycam/mugshot material, was not confirmed as enacted).
notes: The portal's public config endpoint (gaepd.justfoia.com/publicportal/api/configuration) shows isPublicPortalGuestUserEnabled=true and open registration, so an account is optional. The form itself (/Forms/Launch/...) returned a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge (HTTP 403), so I recorded it as blocked and could not see the required fields. A reCAPTCHA client key appears in the portal config, but it is the same key as other JustFOIA tenants, so captcha on the form is unconfirmed.

agency: Hawaii Department of Health (Environmental Health Administration; UIPA requests coordinated by the Compliance, Hearings and Investigations Office)
platform: email / PDF form (OIP 'Request to Access a Government Record')
statute_note: "each agency upon request by any person shall make government records available for inspection and copying". Text read via a search snippet; capitol.hawaii.gov returned a Cloudflare block to me.
notes: The DOH page asks for a written request with 'sufficient contact information'. The OIP form it links says 'Name or Alias' and 'you are not required to provide any personal information', so I recorded name and address as not required. Some environmental branches (HEER, Wastewater, Solid & Hazardous Waste) also have their own request pages. I did not survey those, and HEER mentions an e-Permitting form.

agency: Iowa Department of Natural Resources
statute_note: "Every person shall have the right to examine and copy a public record and to publish or otherwise disseminate a public record"
notes: I rendered the NextRequest form while signed out. Name, Phone, Street address, City, State and Zip are marked required, Email is optional, and I found no captcha element or script. DNR also has a July 2026 procedural rulemaking (567/571 ch. 2, 2505, under 2026 Iowa Acts SF 2463) consolidating its fair-information-practices rules. It is not an intake or ID change.

agency: Idaho Department of Environmental Quality
statute_note: (1) "Every person has a right to examine and take a copy of any public record of this state". But (4) requires each request to include name, mailing address, email and phone, plus "a written declaration by the requesting party attesting or affirming under oath whether such requester is a resident". Residency affects fees only, not the right to request.
change_2026: No 2026 change found. The residency-declaration and contact-info requirements in § 74-102(4) took effect July 1, 2025. DEQ's PDF form, dated January 2026, carries a resident yes/no question 'For tracking purposes only, All requests are processed, regardless of residency'. 2026 bills touched § 74-105 exemptions (S1250), not who may request.
notes: Name, address and residency answers come from DEQ's January 2026 PDF form, which has First/Last Name, Mailing Address and the Idaho-resident Yes/No question, and from § 74-102(4). The JustFOIA config shows guest submission enabled (account optional), but the online form returned a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403), so I could not verify its fields or captcha.

agency: Illinois Environmental Protection Agency
platform: custom web form (IEPA FOIA web app); also fax/mail
statute_note: "Each public body shall make available to any person for inspection or copying all public records, except as otherwise provided in Sections 7 and 8.5 of this Act." ilga.gov timed out for me, so I read this via a search snippet of the official page.
change_2026: Public Act 104-438 (SB 243), effective Jan 1, 2026 (signed Dec 2025), adds FOIA section 3(j): a public body with "a reasonable belief that a request was not submitted by a person may require the requester to verify orally or in writing that the requester is a person"; it may not require personal or identifying information such as a photo ID. Applies to Illinois EPA. Pending 2026 bills on AI-drafted requests did not pass.
notes: Home/Create redirects to Account/Login. The Register page requires First Name, Last Name, Address, City, State, Zip and Phone, and it showed no captcha. The agency page lists no FOIA email and says anonymous requests are accepted only by fax, mail or carrier. 2026 bills on automated or AI requests (HB0031) and recurrent requesters (SB2170, HB4681-4684) were pending or stalled, not enacted.

agency: Indiana Department of Environmental Management (Office of Records Management)
statute_note: "Any person may inspect and copy the public records of any public agency during the regular business hours of the agency". Since July 1, 2026, HEA 1360 lets agencies prioritize Indiana residents and charge non-residents a supplemental fee, but the 'any person' right still stands.
change_2026: HEA 1360 (P.L. 97-2026), signed March 4, 2026 and effective July 1, 2026. It lets agencies run request portals (IC 5-14-3-3.3) that can use CAPTCHA, verify the requester's physical address, check Indiana residency, and track suspected automated, scraping or phishing submissions. It also lets agencies prioritize Indiana-resident and civic, journalistic, academic or personal requests, delay out-of-state and automated requests, charge them a supplemental fee, and deny suspected data-scraping or phishing requests. Agencies must report suspected automated requests to the Public Access Counselor.
notes: The AccessGov form page shows only 'Log in to Start Form', so an account is required, and the fields behind the login could not be seen. idemfileroom@idem.in.gov is published 'for assistance with records requests'. Older State Form 55542 allowed email submission, but the current page points only to the portal, so the email channel is unknown.

agency: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (Division of Environment)
statute_note: "All public records shall be open for inspection by any person, except as otherwise provided by this act"
notes: The KDHE Open Records page and its PDFs returned HTTP 403 (bot block) to both curl and WebFetch. The separate request form loaded without login and marks First/Last Name, Street Address, City, State, Zip, Phone, Email, Division and Signature as required. It ends with a Telerik RadCaptcha ('Type the code from the image') and a K.S.A. 45-230 no-commercial-list attestation. A search snippet attributes kdhe.KORAOfficer@ks.gov to KDHE, but I could not verify it on an agency page, so the email channel is unknown.

agency: Kentucky Energy and Environment Cabinet (Department for Environmental Protection)
statute: KRS 61.872(1)-(2) as amended by 2021 Ky. Acts ch. 160 (HB 312) https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/acts/21RS/documents/0160.pdf
statute_note: "All public records shall be open for inspection by any resident of the Commonwealth"; "Any resident of the Commonwealth shall have the right to inspect public records." The custodian "may require the applicant to provide a statement in the written application of the manner in which the applicant is a resident". The Cabinet's page repeats this, effective June 29, 2021.
change_2026: HB 567 (2026 RS) would have let custodians require government-issued photo ID with an address as proof of residency. It passed the House 71-19 on 3/13/26 and the Senate 28-6 with a substitute on 4/1/26, but was recommitted to House Appropriations & Revenue on 4/15/26 with no further action shown, so it was not enacted per the LRC record.
notes: The DEP PDF form (DEP-0049, a scanned image) has Signature, Company, Address and Phone lines but no residency statement. The Cabinet also offers the AG's standardized form, which I did not open but which per the statute includes a residency statement. The statute lets the custodian require a signed application with a printed name, so name is recorded as yes. Whether the address is mandatory on the form is unclear.

agency: Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality
platform: custom web form (LDEQ EDMS); PDF form ISD-0005-01 by mail/fax
statute_note: "The custodian shall present any public record to any person of the age of majority who so requests. The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who applies for a public record, except an inquiry as to the age and identification..." Residency is required only for records of the governor's office (R.S. 44:31.1).
notes: The EDMS form loads without sign-in ('Sign In' is optional and there is a 'Save this information for next time' box). Step 2 asks for Contact Name, Organization, Email, Mailing Address, City, State, Zip and Phone, with no client-side required markers, so whether name or address is mandatory is unknown. I did not submit. The app bundle sends a reCAPTCHA token (captchaResult) with each create request and shows the Google Privacy/Terms notice, so I recorded captcha as yes (invisible). The agency says emailed requests 'cannot be accepted'; publicrecords@la.gov is for appointments and fee-waiver forms only.

agency: Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection (MassDEP)
platform: custom web form (Gravity Forms on forms.mass.gov)
statute_note: Records access officer "shall ... permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record ... following the receipt of the request". The section puts no residency or citizenship condition on the requester.
notes: WebFetch got a 403 from mass.gov, but plain curl read it. The embedded form marks as required: name, organization (or NA), email, phone and 'Your Address' (street, city, state, zip). No captcha markup in the form HTML. The guidelines page also accepts requests made orally or to program/regional coordinators. Pending S.3244/H.5469 transparency bill (Senate passed 30 July 2026) concerns the Legislature's and Governor's records, not intake. The form is embedded in https://www.mass.gov/forms/massdep-public-records-request-form.

agency: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE)
platform: custom web form (MDE ASP.NET PIA portal)
statute_note: "a custodian shall allow a person or governmental unit to inspect any public record at any reasonable time"
notes: The PIA page says "Please do not submit requests via email", so requests go only through the portal. The portal form marks first/last name, street address, city, state, zip, phone and email as required. It has a 'Requester Type' dropdown that includes 'Citizen' but asks for no residency attestation. No reCAPTCHA markup in the form HTML. 2026 PIA bills found (HB 304 data manipulation; Ch. 880/SB 426 divorce records) do not touch intake.

agency: Maine Department of Environmental Protection
statute_note: "Except as otherwise provided by statute, a person has the right to inspect and copy any public record in accordance with this section within a reasonable time of making the request"
notes: maine.gov (both the DEP page and the state FOAA contact list) returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch. The email and the fact that no form is needed ('There are no required forms') come from search-engine snippets of maine.gov/foaa pages. Name and address are recorded as not required because no form exists, not because I saw a form. The Right to Know Advisory Committee heard testimony in 2026 about AI and bot requests, but I found no enacted intake change (LD 1788 on commercial requesters failed 2/3/2026).

agency: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE)
statute_note: "a person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive copies of the requested public record". A request "must include the requesting person's complete name, address, and contact information". MCL 15.232 excludes people serving a prison sentence from "person".
change_2026: No enacted 2026 change to intake. 2026 FOIA bills (HB 6299, HB 6300, SB 1180, and Senate FOIA expansion to the Legislature and Governor) were still pending or stalled. A Feb 2026 Michigan Advance story reports clerks getting AI-generated bulk FOIA requests, but no rule followed.
notes: michigan.gov returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl. EGLE page text was read from Exa search-index highlights: "Create an account in the EGLE FOIA Request Center to submit", and account creation asks for name, phone and address. Mail and fax are also accepted. The published email is for questions only. The GovQA page is login-gated, so I could not check for a captcha on the request form. Name and address being required comes from both the statute and the account step.

agency: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency (MPCA)
statute_note: "Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data". § 13.05 subd. 12 bars requiring requesters to identify themselves.
change_2026: Statewide procedural change, not about ID or AI: 2025 Minn. Laws ch. 35 added § 13.03 subd. 3(g), reported effective 1 Jan 2026. It lets an entity suspend further response if the requester does not inspect or collect available data within 5 business days. The 2026 session summary lists no intake, identity or AI changes.
notes: pca.state.mn.us served a Radware 'Verifying your browser' challenge, which I did not bypass. MPCA text came from Exa search-index copies of the requests page, the form page and guide e-admin11-20 (Aug 2026). The guide says requesters "must complete and submit the electronic Information request form" and that MPCA "cannot require them to identify themselves". Form fields and captcha could not be seen. The 1 Jan 2026 effective date for subd. 3(g) comes from a search snippet.

agency: Missouri Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
statute_note: "Each public governmental body shall make available for inspection and copying by the public of that body's public records." § 610.011 says records are "open to the public".
notes: The DNR page says to submit "online through the department's Public Records Center system, or by mail". It lists as required "Your name ... mailing address, phone and email". The email is offered for questions. Clicking 'Submit a Request' on the GovQA portal leads to a login/create-account page with no guest option, and the form behind it was not viewed. HB 145 (2025; upfront fees, cancellation for nonpayment) predates 2026. No 2026 Sunshine intake change was found enacted.

agency: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ)
statute_note: "all public records are hereby declared to be public property, and any person shall have the right to inspect, copy" (or reproduce) any public record
notes: The online form requires name, email, phone, company name, full company street address, city, state, zip, subject and details. It loads invisible Google reCAPTCHA (recaptcha/api.js plus a recaptcha_response field). The email address is Cloudflare-obfuscated on the page and I decoded it. The page says requests may be made by mail, email or fax. 2026 PRA bills (HB 1482, SB 2633, HB 1468) died in committee.

agency: Montana Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
platform: statewide portal (ArkCase, run by Office of Public Information Requests)
statute_note: "every person has a right to examine and obtain a copy of any public information of this state" (also Mont. Const. art. II § 9, "No person shall be deprived of the right to examine documents")
notes: deq.mt.gov timed out or returned 503, so DEQ page text came from an Exa search-index copy: "follow the prompts to create an account" and "Why do I have to create an account to request public records?". The OPIR page (doa.mt.gov/OPIR) was read directly and says all requests it handles "must be submitted using one of these methods". ArkCase form fields sit behind account creation and were not viewed.

agency: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
statute_note: "Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined ... by any person". § 132-6(b): no requester "shall be required to disclose the purpose or motive for the request."
notes: DEQ's page says to "provide your name and email address (required)"; phone and organization are optional and no postal address is asked for. The Smartsheet form loads by script and its fields didn't come through, so I couldn't check for a captcha. Smartsheet public forms usually need no login. publicrecords@deq.nc.gov is published for questions and status checks; the page doesn't say it takes requests. The 2025-2026 session laws I found added exemptions (for example NIL contracts and UNC disciplinary records) but didn't change intake.

agency: North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality (NDDEQ)
platform: email only (fillable PDF forms SFN 60237 / SFN 60887)
statute_note: "all records of a public entity are public records, open and accessible for inspection". Agencies "may not ask for the motive or reason for requesting the records or for the identity of the person requesting public records."
notes: There is no online portal: the page says to send requests and questions to DEQOpenRecords@nd.gov and offers fillable PDF forms. The SFN 60237 form says "Requester identification information is not required to fulfill a records request," and the statute bars agencies from asking who you are. Captcha is 'no' because the channel is email or PDF. HB 1306 (2025, fees) failed. No 2026 intake change found.

agency: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE; formerly NDEE)
statute_note: "all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records"
notes: The agency page says requests "must be in writing" by fax, the JustFOIA portal or mail. Email is not listed. The JustFOIA form renders in JavaScript, so I did not see its fields. The portal's public configuration (what the page itself loads) shows guest users and open registration enabled and a reCAPTCHA site key set, so captcha is inferred, not seen. LB525 (approved 14 Apr 2026) adds a records exemption only, not an intake change.

agency: New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services (NHDES)
statute_note: "Every citizen ... has the right to inspect all governmental records". The text says citizen. I found no case or AG opinion saying this word is not enforced. NHDES's portal does not appear to screen for it.
change_2026: Proposed, not enacted: SB 626-FN (2026) would limit right-to-know requests to people domiciled in or with a permanent residence in NH, with proof required (press exception). Senate Judiciary recommended Ought to Pass with Amendment 3-2 on 3/12/2026. It was laid on the table the same day, with no later action.
notes: des.nh.gov returned 403, so the NHDES contact text came from the Exa search index: filereview@des.nh.gov is the "Contact for ... Right to Know request". It is unclear whether that address accepts requests. The JustFOIA public configuration shows guest submission and open registration enabled and a reCAPTCHA key set, so captcha is inferred. Form fields render in JavaScript and were not seen.

agency: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (Office of Record Access)
platform: custom web form (plus paper form by mail)
statute_note: 47:1A-1: records "shall be readily accessible for inspection, copying, or examination by the citizens of this State"; the other sections say "any person"/"requestor". Scheeler v. Atlantic County MJIF, 454 N.J. Super. 621 (App. Div. 2018) held out-of-state requestors have standing, so the citizen wording is not enforced. Answered yes only because the text says "citizens".
notes: The online form marks First/Last Name, Affiliation/Company, Street Address, City, State, Zip, Daytime Phone and the request text as required (*). Email is optional. The address block is split into NJ residents and non-NJ residents, so it asks where you live but doesn't limit who can ask. It also requires an answer, under penalty of N.J.S.A. 2C:28-3, to whether you have been convicted of an indictable offense, plus your initials. The agency says requests must come through the online form or by paper mail. Curl was blocked by Incapsula; I read the page with WebFetch. I couldn't see whether there is a captcha. No 2026 intake change found; the last overhaul was P.L.2024 c.16.

agency: New Mexico Environment Department (NMED)
statute_note: "every person has the right to inspect public records of this state". NMED's notice repeats it: "every person has the right to inspect public records of the New Mexico Environment Department".
change_2026: Proposed only, nothing enacted: the IPRA Task Force set up under HJM 2 reported to the Legislature in October 2026 ('Safeguarding Sunshine'). Approved recommendation 7 would make out-of-state requesters pay the actual cost of reviewing body-camera footage. AI, bot and automated requesters, along with vexatious and batch requesters, were raised in public comment, but the Task Force made no recommendation on them. No enacted 2026 change to ID, verification or account rules found.
notes: The NMED page returned 503 to WebFetch and curl; I read it through the Exa fetch and search copy. The page says the JustFOIA portal needs no account and that a request "must contain the name, address and telephone number". The portal form loads by script, so I didn't see its fields or whether it has a captcha. The current page lists mail, phone and the portal but no email; the address comes from NMED's 2024 IPRA request form (Attachment A PDF). I couldn't open the statute on nmonesource (403), so the wording comes from NMED's notice, which quotes it.

agency: Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP)
platform: custom web form (plus PDF form by mail)
statute_note: public records "must be open at all times during office hours to inspection by any person"
change_2026: No enacted change. The AB 128 (2025) Public Records Task Force met through 2026 on 'broad' requests and redaction burden. A draft recommendation would require a human-reviewed response within 5 business days, not just an automated email. Final report was due 31 Oct 2026.
notes: The page says: "You will need to provide your name and email address". The online form fields are name, date, company, phone, email, confirm email, bureau and description, with no postal address field. No captcha markup found. Written requests go by mail to the Records Request Coordinator. No email intake address is published.

agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC), Records Access Office
statute_note: "Each agency shall, in accordance with its published rules, make available for public inspection and copying all records". There are no residency or citizenship words.
notes: GovQA's 'Submit a FOIL Request' opens a login page that says "If this is your first online request, please create an account". DEC's FAQ puts Create Account before the request form, so an account looks required for the portal, but no page says so outright. I didn't create an account, so the request-form fields and any captcha are unknown. DEC's page says the PDF Application for Access to Records can be emailed, mailed or faxed. No 2026 change to verification or AI rules found; S9607, on electronic FOIL appeals, died in 2026.

agency: Ohio Environmental Protection Agency (Ohio EPA)
platform: custom web form (online file review checklist; loads by script, URL not seen)
statute_note: "Upon request from any person" records must be promptly prepared. (B)(4): "any requirement that the requester disclose the requester's identity or the intended use" is treated as a denial.
notes: Ohio EPA's page says "you do not even need to provide your identity," a written request isn't required, and use of the online checklist form is optional. Curl got a 404, so I read the page through Exa. I couldn't find the form's URL or fields. The page lists named staff email addresses for the central and district offices, but I found no role address, so the address field is left blank. Section 149.43 was amended in 2025-2026 (HB 96, and HB 31 effective 2026-09-07), but those changes cover exemptions, video fees and parole records, not intake or ID.

agency: Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), Central Records
statute_note: "All records of public bodies and public officials shall be open to any person for inspection, copying, or mechanical reproduction". Since SB 535 (effective 2025-11-01), ¶7 says "A public body may require a requestor to complete a records request form" and requires reasonable specificity.
notes: The form's iframe marks First Name, Last Name, Email, Subject and the request message as mandatory. It has fields for phone and attachments and none for postal address. I saw no captcha in the static form markup, but one could be added at runtime, so I marked it unknown. Neither the records page nor the contact page publishes a request email. Not 2026: SB 535 (2025) added advance fees over $75, permission to require agency forms, and a specificity standard. In 2026, SB 1532 would have let agencies require a requester's full name and contact details; it died on 2026-05-14.

agency: Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
statute_note: "Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state", except as ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355 provide.
notes: ordeq.org/publicrecords redirects to GovQA. The portal's FAQ is titled "Why do I have to create an account to request records?" and says that when you register, "an email or mailing address is the only required detail", so I marked account yes, name no and postal address no. Requests can also go by postal mail. The email address is published "for any additional questions"; the page doesn't say it takes requests. The Public Records Advisory Council's 2026 work (draft report, 2027 bill ideas) is still at proposal stage.

agency: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP), Agency Open Records Officer
platform: custom web form (plus OOR standard form by email or mail)
statute_note: "Requester" means "A person that is a legal resident of the United States and requests a record pursuant to this act." That limits requesters to US residents, not PA residents. § 703: a written request "shall include the name and address to which the agency should address its response." (Limit is to legal residents of the United States, not of Pennsylvania; coded us_only.)
change_2026: Proposed only, nothing enacted: SB 431 (Pennycuick) would let agencies reject requests "automatically generated" by AI on "reasonable suspicion"; it was laid on the table 2026-02-04. SB 790 on vexatious requesters left a Senate committee in June 2026. OOR guidance says AI-drafted requests can't be denied for that reason at present. No enacted 2026 change found.
notes: The DEP form needs "Either Requester's Address or Requester's E-Mail", so a postal address isn't mandatory. It has a checkbox: "I affirm that my full name and contact information is true and correct, and that I am a legal resident of the United States"; leaving it unchecked "may result in the denial of my request". That is a US-residency attestation, not a PA one. Name is marked yes because of that affirmation and § 703; the asterisks didn't show in the copy I read. The form returned 503 to WebFetch and failed TLS in curl, so I read it through Exa and couldn't check for a captcha.

agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM), Office of Customer & Technical Assistance
statute_note: "every person or entity shall have the right to inspect and/or copy those records". Under (j), a public body may not require a requester to "provide personally identifiable information about him/herself."
change_2026: Proposed only, nothing enacted: H 7985 (introduced 2026-02-27, sent to House State Government & Elections) would require "sufficient identifying information to permit verification of the requester's identity", at minimum a name plus a mailing or email address, and says "Anonymous public records requests shall not be accepted or processed." I found no sign it passed.
notes: dem.ri.gov returned 403 to WebFetch and curl; I read the page and PDF form through the Exa fetch copy. The DEM form labels "REQUESTOR'S INFORMATION: (OPTIONAL)" and the signature as optional. dem.ri.gov/publicrequest is a separate Marine Fisheries data-request form, not the general APRA channel. Captcha is 'no' because the channel is a PDF form or email.

agency: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (SCDES)
statute_note: "A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record"; the right does not extend to people serving a prison sentence.
notes: The JustFOIA portal home page has a 'Sign in' link and a reCAPTCHA badge, and lets you track a request by request number and security key (so an account looks optional). The actual form (des-sc.justfoia.com/Forms/Launch/...) was behind a Cloudflare bot check and was not read, so required fields are unknown. The PDF form D-2295 for email/fax/mail asks for name and street address and a Family Privacy Protection Act signature, but does not mark them required. The old IQ eForm now redirects to the new process.

agency: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources (DANR)
platform: statewide portal (sd.gov Citizen Services, ServiceNow-style service portal)
statute_note: "all citizens of this state, and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to examine such public record"
notes: DANR's home page 'Request Public Records' link goes to the statewide sd.gov Public Records Request Portal (pick an agency, describe the records, 10 business day response). The fields only appear after pressing 'Submit Record Request', which I did not press, so account, fields and captcha are unknown. The portal nav shows 'My Requests'/'My Payments', which suggests accounts exist. No captcha was visible on the landing page. No DANR-specific records email found. 2026 HB 1092 only added exemptions, not intake rules.

agency: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC)
platform: email / mail with rule-prescribed request form
statute_note: "open for personal inspection by any citizen of this state"; the custodian may require government photo ID with an address, or other proof of Tennessee residency.
change_2026: Pub. Ch. 711 (2026) (HB 1911/SB 1970), effective 7/1/2026, lets a non-citizen of Tennessee inspect or get a copy of a law enforcement record about only that person. This narrowly loosens the citizenship limit statewide but does not affect TDEC environmental records.
notes: TDEC's page is being reorganized and only links Rule 0400-01-01 (the PDF link returned an error page). The details come from the rule text on Cornell LII: copy requests must be written on the Public Records Request Form, sent by email or mail. The form has a 'Tennessee citizen? Yes/No' checkbox and name/contact fields. The rule lets TDEC ask for government photo ID (discretionary, not a form field). A search snippet showed Public.Records.Request@tn.gov, but the rule text says TDEC.Public.Records.Request@tn.gov.

agency: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ)
statute: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.021 (and § 552.234 on request methods) https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/GV/htm/GV.552.htm
statute_note: "Public information is available to the public"; § 552.234: "A person may make a written request" by mail, email, hand delivery or another approved method. § 552.222 allows asking only to "establish proper identification".
notes: The PIRCS form (3 pages, 120-minute session) needs no login. Its help text says mailing address is required only when delivery is by mail, and contact/delivery preference is required. Name has no required marker. Page 1 had no captcha, but I did not reach later pages. TCEQ says it need not respond to requests sent by other channels or addresses. HB 4219 (eff. 9/1/2025) changed response duties, not intake.

agency: Utah Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
email_address: edograma@utah.gov (department-wide); division addresses ddwgrama@utah.gov, errgrama@utah.gov, wmrcgrama@utah.gov, wqgrama@utah.gov
statute_note: "a person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge"; § 63G-2-204 requires a written request with "name, mailing address, daytime phone number".
notes: The DEQ page says GRAMA requires name, mailing address, daytime phone and a description, and points to a GRAMA PDF form (Laserfiche-hosted). Requests go by email to the division. I did not open the PDF itself, so whether it asks about residency is unknown. A new version of § 63G-2-201 takes effect 7/1/2026, but the text I read still says 'a person' (the vexatious-requester limits date from 2025). I found no 2026 intake or ID change. The 2026 GRAMA bills I checked (SB 64, HB 551) appear not to have passed or don't concern intake.

agency: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
statute_note: "all public records shall be open to citizens of the Commonwealth, representatives of newspapers and magazines with circulation in the Commonwealth, and representatives of radio and television stations broadcasting in or into the Commonwealth"; "The custodian may require the requester to provide his name and legal address."
notes: The NextRequest form loads without login ('Sign in' optional). Its HTML marks Name, Phone, Street address, City, State and Zip as required (only State shows a visible asterisk), and Email is not required. The State dropdown lists all states, with no residency attestation. No captcha element found. The DEQ FOIA page itself was blocked (Akamai 403), so whether email is a current channel is unknown; regional FOIA emails exist only on 2013 archive pages. The FOIA Council's 2026 update lists 15 FOIA bills, none changing who may request or intake ID. AI requests are only under FOIA Council study (July 2026).

agency: Vermont Agency of Natural Resources, Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
email_address: ANR.WMPDFOIA@vermont.gov (Waste Management Division); other DEC records officers and liaisons have named-person addresses
statute_note: "Any person may inspect or copy any public record of a public agency"
notes: anr.vermont.gov and dec.vermont.gov returned CloudFront 403 to both curl and a headless browser, so I did not get around the block. The page contents come from Exa search highlights: an online form with 'Requestor Information' and 'Request Details' sections, plus email to records officers and liaisons. Form fields, captcha and account are not visible. account_required 'no' is inferred from email being allowed.

agency: Washington State Department of Ecology
statute_note: "make them promptly available to any person"; "Agencies shall not distinguish among persons requesting records"; existing (3) lets agencies deny multiple "bot request[s]" within 24 hours.
notes: GovQA 'Submit Request' redirects to a login/create-account page ('If this is your first online request, please create an account'), so the online channel needs an account. Email and mail stay open. I did not view the post-login form fields. The ecology.wa.gov page returned 403 to curl but was read via WebFetch. 2026 HB 1964 (bot requests) and the other PRA intake bills died; the bot-request clause in RCW 42.56.080(3) dates from 2017.

agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
statute_note: "any requester has a right to inspect any record"; (1)(i): no request "may be refused because the person making the request is unwilling to be identified or to state the purpose of the request".
notes: DNR prefers email, accepts requests in any format and says the form is optional. Name/address 'no' rests on the page plus § 19.35(1)(i) anonymity; the XFA PDF form could not be parsed. The legislature site timed out, so the statute text came from Exa's copy of docs.legis.wisconsin.gov and Justia (2025). Wisconsin DOJ says the law does not address AI requests, and I found no 2026 change.

agency: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection (WVDEP)
statute_note: "Every person has a right to inspect or copy any public record of a public body in this state" (statute site returned 503; wording confirmed via search of the official code site).
notes: The embedded ColdFusion/Lucee form asks for name, address, city, state, zip, phone and email. Its client-side validation marks every field not-required (addInput(...,false,...)), and server-side checks are unknown. No captcha or login. The email address comes from search snippets of the DEP site. 2026 HB 4163 (hide requester names in FOIA logs) stalled in committee.

agency: Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ)
statute_note: "All public records shall be open for inspection by any person at reasonable times"
notes: The NextRequest form loads without login (an account is created on submission: 'After signing up and submitting your request'). Its HTML marks name, phone, city, zip and state as required, and email as not required. No captcha. The DEQ page names only the online form, with no records email. 2026 SF0049 (PRA revisions: timelines and fees) failed introduction 15-16 on 2/9/2026.
